input.details:
S-103 Castellan Excipients will miss its next RM-103 shipment (PO000210, 3,300 units, promised 2026-10-03) by about 4 weeks, to about 2026-10-31. Its later open POs PO000211/212/213 (4,400/2,200/5,900, promised 10-10/10-18/10-25) may slip too; please confirm with the supplier.

RM-103 is used in Lacrivia FG-1001/1002 and Cyclosporine FG-1003, all made at PL-01 (via SEMI-044/045). It is also used in Oculon FG-2001/2002, made at PL-02 (via CMP-320 > SEMI-060).

Mitigation done: PR-06C2EF77 raised to S-111 Kingsley Excipients for 2,800 units to PL-01, need-by 2026-10-03.

GAP: In the supplier portal, S-111 is approved for RM-103 only at PL-01, not PL-02. S-103 is the only approved source for PL-02. The PL-02 share of the delayed quantity is about 500 units (about 16%, estimated from BOM-weighted 13-week FG demand).

Requested actions:
(1) Ask S-103 to expedite or send a partial shipment of at least the PL-02 quantity ahead of the rest, and confirm revised dates for PO000210 through PO000213.
(2) Quality to assess whether S-111 can be urgently approved for PL-02.
(3) PL-02 to confirm RM-103 on-hand coverage; SUPPLY_DEMO has no plant raw-material inventory.

Context: Oculon DC stock is currently above safety stock at all DCs. Lacrivia at DC-EAST is already below safety stock (FG-1001 46 vs SS 471; FG-1002 34 vs SS 233), so PL-01 supply is the more critical.

RM-103 is used in Lacrivia FG-1001/1002 and Cyclosporine FG-1003, all made at PL-01 (via SEMI-044/045). It is also used in Oculon FG-2001/2002, made at PL-02 (via CMP-320 > SEMI-060).

Mitigation done: PR-06C2EF77 raised to S-111 Kingsley Excipients for 2,800 units to PL-01, need-by 2026-10-03.

GAP: In the supplier portal, S-111 is approved for RM-103 only at PL-01, not PL-02. S-103 is the only approved source for PL-02. The PL-02 share of the delayed quantity is about 500 units (about 16%, estimated from BOM-weighted 13-week FG demand).

Requested actions:
(1) Ask S-103 to expedite or send a partial shipment of at least the PL-02 quantity ahead of the rest, and confirm revised dates for PO000210 through PO000213.
(2) Quality to assess whether S-111 can be urgently approved for PL-02.
(3) PL-02 to confirm RM-103 on-hand coverage; SUPPLY_DEMO has no plant raw-material inventory.

Context: Oculon DC stock is currently above safety stock at all DCs. Lacrivia at DC-EAST is already below safety stock (FG-1001 46 vs SS 471; FG-1002 34 vs SS 233), so PL-01 supply is the more critical.

text:
I raised a 2,800-unit requisition to our backup supplier for one plant, but the other plant has no approved backup, so its share is with Procurement / Supplier Quality.

**What's affected**
- S-103 (Castellan) is our main supplier for RM-103 (glycerin). Its next open shipment is PO000210: 3,300 units promised for 2026-10-03, now expected around 2026-10-31. It also has three later open orders (PO000211, 212 and 213, due Oct 10–25), which could slip too.
- RM-103 goes into all five finished products:
  - **Plant PL-01 (Riverside):** Lacrivia 5 mL and 10 mL, and Cyclosporine 0.05%.
  - **Plant PL-02 (Lakeview):** Oculon 2.5 mL and 5 mL.
- The only other qualified supplier is S-111 (Kingsley). The supplier portal shows it active but approved to ship RM-103 only to PL-01. PL-02 has no approved backup.

**Actions taken**
1. **Purchase requisition PR-06C2EF77:** 2,800 units of RM-103 from S-111, delivered to PL-01, need-by 2026-10-03, marked to expedite. 2,800 is PL-01's estimated share (about 84%) of the delayed 3,300.
2. **Case CASE-E6241C73 for Procurement / Supplier Quality.** It asks them to:
   - get S-103 to rush a partial shipment of at least PL-02's share (about 500 units) and confirm new dates for PO000210–213;
   - have Quality check whether S-111 can be approved quickly for PL-02;
   - have PL-02 confirm how much RM-103 it has on hand.

**Not done, and why**
- **No order for PL-02:** S-111 isn't approved to ship there, so I gave that to the case owners rather than work around the approval.
- **Lacrivia stock at our East warehouse (DC-EAST) was not acted on:** it is already below safety stock and has dropped every week since mid-August (FG-1001: 46 units vs 471 safety stock; FG-1002: 34 vs 233). This started before the RM-103 slip, but the slip adds risk to Lacrivia supply. Splitting stock between customers or moving it from another warehouse needs the Supply Planning lead's approval and wasn't part of this task. Do you want me to prepare that?
- **No customer or wholesaler notices:** no finished-goods shortage from this delay has been confirmed yet.

**Assumptions**
- "Next shipment" means PO000210 only. The later orders are flagged in the case but not covered.
- Our purchase orders don't say which plant they ship to, and the data has no plant-level raw-material stock. So I split the 3,300 between plants using the last 13 weeks of finished-goods demand multiplied by the recipe quantities. This is an estimate, not a confirmed split.
- S-111 usually ships about 23 days after ordering, so 2026-10-03 is the date we need the material, not one it can likely meet. It should still arrive well before 2026-10-31.

question: Supplier S-103 will miss its next RM-103 shipment by four weeks. Handle it.

sql.sql: SELECT * FROM dbo.PURCH_ORD WHERE MATERIAL_ID='RM-103' ORDER BY ORDER_DT DESC

SELECT sm.SUPPLIER_ID, sm.MATERIAL_ID, sm.QUALIFIED_FLG, sm.PRIMARY_FLG, s.SUPPLIER_NM, s.COUNTRY, s.TIER, m.MATERIAL_DESC, m.MATERIAL_TYP FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL sm LEFT JOIN dbo.SUPPLIER s ON s.SUPPLIER_ID=sm.SUPPLIER_ID LEFT JOIN dbo.MATERIAL m ON m.MATERIAL_ID=sm.MATERIAL_ID WHERE sm.MATERIAL_ID='RM-103'

WITH x AS (SELECT PARENT_MATERIAL_ID, CHILD_MATERIAL_ID, QTY_PER, EFF_FROM, EFF_TO, 1 AS lvl FROM dbo.BOM WHERE CHILD_MATERIAL_ID='RM-103' UNION ALL SELECT b.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID, b.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID, b.QTY_PER, b.EFF_FROM, b.EFF_TO, x.lvl+1 FROM dbo.BOM b JOIN x ON b.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID=x.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID WHERE x.lvl<10) SELECT x.*, m.MATERIAL_DESC, m.MATERIAL_TYP FROM x LEFT JOIN dbo.MATERIAL m ON m.MATERIAL_ID=x.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID ORDER BY lvl

SELECT b1.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID p1, m1.MATERIAL_DESC d1, b1.QTY_PER q1, b1.EFF_FROM f1, b1.EFF_TO t1, b2.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID p2, m2.MATERIAL_DESC d2, b2.QTY_PER q2, b2.EFF_TO t2, b3.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID p3, m3.MATERIAL_DESC d3, b3.QTY_PER q3, b3.EFF_TO t3, b4.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID p4, b4.QTY_PER q4, b4.EFF_TO t4
FROM dbo.BOM b1 LEFT JOIN dbo.MATERIAL m1 ON m1.MATERIAL_ID=b1.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID
LEFT JOIN dbo.BOM b2 ON b2.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID=b1.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID LEFT JOIN dbo.MATERIAL m2 ON m2.MATERIAL_ID=b2.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID
LEFT JOIN dbo.BOM b3 ON b3.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID=b2.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID LEFT JOIN dbo.MATERIAL m3 ON m3.MATERIAL_ID=b3.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID
LEFT JOIN dbo.BOM b4 ON b4.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID=b3.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID
WHERE b1.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID='RM-103'

SELECT pm.PLANT_ID, pm.MATERIAL_ID, p.* FROM dbo.PLANT_MATERIAL pm LEFT JOIN dbo.PLANT p ON p.PLANT_ID=pm.PLANT_ID WHERE pm.MATERIAL_ID IN ('RM-103','CMP-320','SEMI-060','SEMI-044','SEMI-045','FILL-1001','FILL-1002','FILL-1003','FILL-2001','FILL-2002','FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002') ORDER BY pm.MATERIAL_ID
SELECT i.DC_ID, i.MATERIAL_ID, i.SNAPSHOT_DT, i.ON_HAND_UNITS, i.SAFETY_STOCK_UNITS FROM dbo.DC_INV i WHERE i.SNAPSHOT_DT=(SELECT MAX(SNAPSHOT_DT) FROM dbo.DC_INV) ORDER BY i.MATERIAL_ID, i.DC_ID

SELECT DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID, SUM(UNITS) units_13wk, SUM(UNITS)/13.0 avg_wk, MIN(SHIP_DT) mn, MAX(SHIP_DT) mx FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP WHERE SHIP_DT > DATEADD(week,-13,'2026-09-30') GROUP BY DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID ORDER BY MATERIAL_ID, DC_ID

SELECT DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID, SNAPSHOT_DT, ON_HAND_UNITS, SAFETY_STOCK_UNITS FROM dbo.DC_INV WHERE DC_ID='DC-EAST' AND MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002') AND SNAPSHOT_DT>='2026-07-01' ORDER BY MATERIAL_ID, SNAPSHOT_DT
